correctness.rationale: For any coloured induced support of order s with largest part size a, every colour class has size at least (s-a+1)/2, forcing k<=max(2,a). An optimal M>=3 colour support thus contains a full largest part A. With t outsiders, M ceil((t+1)/2)<=M+t implies t(M-2)<=M. Integer and local coloured-closed-neighbourhood quorum checks eliminate t>0 for M>=4 and leave precisely t=0,1,3 for M=3. For t=3 all classes are crossing pairs, and outsiders must fill a second entire triple part. Necessity and sufficiency are proved in RESULT.md. Counting disjoint types gives p, 3p(N-3), 6 C(p,2). The accompanying independent direct enumerator checked all claimed optimum supports and counts for 66 finite labelled part profiles; finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary preprint proves only the optimal colour count M on complete multipartite graphs and provides a necessary class-size bound. Its inspected Definition 2.2, Theorem 6.4 and corresponding proof do not classify every attaining support or enumerate solutions. The present theorem additionally proves that supports beyond one full maximum part exist exactly when M=3, identifies all such configurations and gives the exact named-colour count M!p(3N+3p-11) for M=3 and M!p for M>=4. Full-support quorum colourings are logically different. Semantic searches of published mathematical records found no stated equivalent; searches cannot certify global uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unstated or previously unindexed exact equality-case enumeration may exist in other literature.

value.rationale: It determines the entire attaining assignment space of an independently motivated new partial-colouring parameter on a natural infinite family, rather than a routine numerical optimization. The phase transition at largest-part size four is rigid: arbitrary other coloured vertices are impossible, whereas three-part maxima permit precisely two additional structural types. The exact polynomial p(3N+3p-11) identifies nontrivial dependence on the count of maximum parts and allows exact sampling or orbit studies; the full-support scalar optimum by itself does not provide these data.
